scope: Ten original biological papers; currently viewed figure assets and separately qualified author-code parameters. Layout/mark grammar only.
parameter_policy: Numeric defaults in bf_mark_style are BioFigure design starting values, not journal mandates or inferred published-panel measurements.

metadata.title: SCENIC+: single-cell multiomic inference of enhancers and gene regulatory networks
metadata.metadata_verification: Official publisher article read via web; published 13 July 2023.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2125x2157 to 1568x1591.
observations: Thin colored vertical highlight bands span aligned genomic tracks. Black coverage traces remain visible through them.
Regional bands have lower visual weight than the evidence traces, while region-gene arcs use a separate blue score legend.
Track windows and x coordinates are shared; local labels and legends sit in reserved whitespace.
figure_observation.caption_support: Official Figure 2 caption explicitly describes predicted target sites using colored ticks and semi-transparent boxes.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2168x1745 to 1749x1408.
observations: Distribution panel uses pale small observations under clearly outlined boxes and dark central summaries.
PCA perturbation panels use many pale short arrows as context with a few stronger arrows visible; colored cell clusters and labels retain identity.
Schematic, distributions, embeddings and heatmap use different visual weights according to role.

additional_author_code.layer: sns.stripplot dark observation points over violin
additional_author_code.mapping: Author source proves this layer setting. Its historical file numbering differs from the inspected final main figures; exact final panel mapping is unverified.

unverified_boundaries: Numeric alpha for Figure 2g bands and Figure 4e/f marks is unknown.
Arrow darkness in Figure 4f can encode distance traveled, as the official caption states; do not treat it as aesthetic alpha alone.
Gene-network and prediction outputs require their original biological/statistical contracts.
transfer_suggestion: Use low-opacity regional fills behind aligned genomic evidence, preserving black track readability.
Give dense contextual observations less visual weight than outlines and summaries.
Declare whether arrow/edge darkness encodes a variable before applying aesthetic transparency.

metadata.title: Multi-omics single-cell data integration and regulatory inference with graph-linked embedding
metadata.metadata_verification: Official publisher article read via web; published 2 May 2022.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2117x1038 to 2048x1004.
observations: Three modalities share embedding geometry; sparse marks can be larger while the denser RNA marks remain small.
Dashed cluster loops highlight groups without filling their interior.
Boxplots have clear black boundaries and white-centered black-outlined mean triangles.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2114x1474 to 1881x1312.
observations: Dense joint scatter uses small visually quiet points under stronger unfilled density contours.
Marginal density plots use pale overlapping filled areas with clear colored boundary curves.
ROC curves remain clearly visible; a light dashed diagonal supports the interpretation.
Density panels occupy their own gutters and share axes with the central plot, preventing overlap.

author_outline.mapping: Matches Figure 3f plot variable, omics-layer order and ylabel. Final composite export not rerun.

additional_author_code.mapping: Author correlation-comparison output corr_cmp.pdf; not proof of Figure 4b exact alpha.

unverified_boundaries: Figure 4b marginal fill opacity is unknown; it may use package defaults or postprocessing.
White-centered mean markers are proven in source; they are mean summaries, not a mandate to outline every dense cell.
Draw order and alpha affect apparent category mixing in embeddings.
transfer_suggestion: Use small translucent points for dense clouds, readable contour lines for distribution structure and low-opacity marginal fill.
Use fill and stroke independently for modest-sized highlighted or summary markers.
Reserve dedicated marginal/legend gutters; maintain consistent limits across matched embeddings.

metadata.title: Haplotype-aware analysis of somatic copy number variations from single-cell transcriptomes
metadata.metadata_verification: Official publisher search result confirms Nature Biotechnology 41, 417-426 (2023), online publication 26 September 2022.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2115x2663 to 1408x1772.
observations: Dense neutral genomic observations appear as a quiet grey field behind strong black/blue segment estimates.
Genomic tracks are stacked with shared chromosome boundaries and coordinate extent; the legend is outside the data.
Precision-recall panel uses visible colored sample points; violin panel uses strong black individual points over colored distributions and a dark summary line.
This paper intentionally mixes weak background marks and opaque foreground observations.

author_layers.layer: WGS BAF background points in author plot_purple function
author_layers.mapping: Function displays per-chromosome BAF data with overlaid opaque blue segment estimates, matching Figure 2a grammar. Exact final sample-specific export unverified.

author_layers.layer: CNV AUC per-sample jitter points over violin
author_layers.mapping: Matches Figure 2e AUC/method violin and individual-point grammar. Final composite export not rerun.

unverified_boundaries: Background alpha=0.02 is an extreme high-density WGS setting, not a universal point default.
The plotting function includes subsampling sample_frac(0.2); density and alpha must be evaluated together.
Some genomic mark colors encode CNV state, so fading those layers indiscriminately could weaken state discrimination.
transfer_suggestion: Use a low-contrast dense background cloud plus clear segment estimates in genomic plots.
Keep low-n observations identifiable; opaque points are appropriate when they are sparse and form primary evidence.
Make opacity conditional on local density, visual role and final physical size.

metadata.title: scBasset: sequence-based modeling of single-cell ATAC-seq using convolutional neural networks
metadata.authors: Han Yuan and David R. Kelley
metadata.metadata_verification: Official publisher search result and PubMed 35941239 verify title/DOI and 2022 Sep;19(9):1088-1096. Publisher live open redirects to inaccessible cookie endpoint; no bypass attempted.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2119x1061 to 2048x1025.
observations: Large dense single-cell plots use small marks; low-count method comparison points use explicit direct labels.
Matched UMAPs share a repeated panel grammar with separate compact legends.
Integration boxplots are white-filled with black outlines and strong central medians.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2120x1705 to 1750x1408.
observations: Neutral grey scatter points permit selected TF labels in red to stand out.
Precision-recall lines have crisp group colors and separate annotation space.
Small grouped violins combine colored bodies, dark outlines and visible individual observations; significance brackets occupy a planned upper lane.

code_confirmed_alpha.source_status: Existing author motif/ISM notebooks and embedding examples inspected by text search; no verified numeric alpha binding to these selected panels.

unverified_boundaries: Pastel UMAP hues do not prove translucency; alpha remains unknown.
White-filled integration boxplots are hollow geometries; they need not be implemented by reducing alpha.
Source-gene labels, TF activity correlations and significance brackets retain their biological meanings.
transfer_suggestion: Choose marker size/density first, then tune alpha if overplotting remains.
Use outlined distribution geometry or outlined focus markers to keep the light field readable.
Keep aggregate curves crisp and reserve bracket/legend lanes before rendering.

metadata.title: A draft human pangenome reference
metadata.metadata_verification: Official publisher article and Figure 2 caption read via web.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image fresh inspection on 2026-10-13; tool displayed full figure, resized from 2161x1171 to 2048x1110.
observations: Annotation percentages show separate assembly observations, with a small orange comparison-reference point.
Copy-number panels place pale grey bars behind stronger blue bubbles, producing a clear evidence hierarchy.
Blue bubble sizes have a count meaning; supporting bars and focal observations are distinct layers.
Legends, axis labels and panels use whitespace and aligned baselines; semantically comparable marks retain colors across panels.

code_confirmed_alpha.source_status: Associated RNA analysis repository does not bind Figure 2 generation; no numeric alpha inferred.

unverified_boundaries: Pale grey bars and light-colored point groups may use lighter base colors rather than alpha.
Point size is quantitative in panels d/e; do not change size for decoration.
The figure provides layout and hierarchy evidence, not numerical transparency evidence.
transfer_suggestion: Use neutral, light supporting bars behind a stronger point layer when the two encodings have separate declared meanings.
Separate foreground/background color and opacity decisions.
Preserve quantitative point-size scale and clear legend while using restrained supportive fills.

metadata.title: Conserved properties of dentate gyrus neurogenesis across postnatal development revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing
metadata.metadata_verification: Current publisher search result confirms title, DOI, 21:290-299 and 15 January 2018 publication; local pinned source manifest agrees.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image; actual current visual inspection; tool resized the 2125x2264 source to 1531x1632 for display

observations.observation: Thin pale gray graph connections sit behind small, stronger categorical cell points; cell-type labels occupy open areas next to clusters.
Six gene views reuse one embedding; a light gray context cloud and gray graph scaffold allow red expression highlights to remain the focal layer.
Cyan and dark purple focal progenitor points are larger and stronger than the gray surrounding trajectory; an explicit black separator is used for a biological boundary.
Repeated age and gene embedding panels share geometry, with small black or red foreground points over subdued gray context.

author_layers.binding: Related early-neurogenesis graph renderer; same graph-and-cell visual grammar, exact final Figure 2 assembly not independently rerun or fully bound.

unverified_boundaries: Edge alpha 0.8 combines with a pale gray edge color; visual attenuation cannot be attributed to alpha alone.
Graph edges and node marks have separate roles; no numerical claim about published node opacity.
Do not require dark outlines on every tiny single-cell point: their summed edge area can dominate the density cloud.
transfer_suggestion: Draw context connections first, pale and thin; then focal points and labels.
Reuse identical embedding coordinates, limits and point scale across gene/age views.
Use separate opacity controls for context, raw observations and highlights; evaluate crowding at final physical size.

metadata.title: Single cell transcriptomics identifies a signaling network coordinating endoderm and mesoderm diversification during foregut organogenesis
metadata.metadata_verification: Current original Nature PDF search result and local Europe PMC article XML confirm title, journal, 11:4158 and 27 August 2020.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image; actual current visual inspection; tool resized the 1946x2507 source to 1391x1792 for display

observations.observation: Predicted interactions use black arrows for strong signal and gray arrows for moderate signal, as explicitly stated by the legend; circular mark size encodes expressing-cell percentage and color encodes normalized expression.
Fine gray connections lie under warm-colored expression points; the two embeddings are balanced in size and their gradient scale is compact.
Black solid paths and gray dashed paths create a clear trajectory hierarchy; categorical stage-node circles have thin gray outlines and restrained fill.

unverified_boundaries: Gray versus black interaction edges encode evidence strength; reducing edge opacity uniformly would erase that hierarchy.
Expression bubble hue has a numeric legend; arbitrary opacity scaling by group would change perceived expression.
The published expression ramp includes red/green and should not become a color-vision-safe BioFigure default.
transfer_suggestion: Give predicted interaction confidence an explicit, stable line grammar.
Use thin circular outlines for moderately sized schematic or categorical nodes; keep them subordinate to data and labels.
Keep marker-size and expression-color keys outside the active network area.

metadata.title: Multimodal spatiotemporal phenotyping of human retinal organoid development
metadata.metadata_verification: Current original publisher result confirms 8 May 2023, 41:1765-1775; local article XML agrees.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image; actual current visual inspection; tool resized the 2163x1017 source to 2048x963 for display

observations.observation: A dense pale gray GRN scaffold supports a small set of stronger red/blue nodes; the focal OTX2 node is larger and black, and a short label leader separates its text.
Categorical boxplot fills are bounded by thin black edges, with black medians and whiskers; those summary marks remain readable in compact panels.
Focal perturbation cells are small colored points over a pale gray embedding; foreground and background do not share the same visual strength.
Many dark observation points accumulate around the origin; a thin fitted diagonal and unobtrusive dashed zero lines remain discernible, with selected labels moved into empty areas.

author_layers.binding: Author plotting utility verified; exact Fig. 6b/f call and final panel alpha not bound in this review.

unverified_boundaries: Alpha 0.8 is a repository utility parameter, not a confirmed opacity measurement for every inspected panel.
Zero-valued observations use a separate neutral context color in the utility; do not use opacity to suppress valid high or low observations selectively.
The strong black summary edges should stay visually distinct from attenuated context.
transfer_suggestion: Separate pale context edges from colored focal nodes.
Keep medians, whiskers and box boundaries at stable visible opacity; use restrained fill for distribution shapes.
For moderate scatter size, offer partially transparent fill plus a thin edge, with edge thickness scaled to final physical point diameter.

metadata.title: Elucidating Human Milk Oligosaccharide biosynthetic genes through network-based multi-omics integration
metadata.metadata_verification: Current publisher and PMC original-article search results confirm title and DOI; local source manifest binds year 2022 and publisher Fig.5 asset.

figure_observation.method: functions.view_image; actual current visual inspection of retained original Figure5.png; publisher URL cross-checked against locally preserved publisher article HTML

observations.observation: Four colored profiles use solid versus dashed lines to distinguish cohorts; a shared legend is outside the plot, while the categorical x-axis compares three model metrics.
A low-density field of small dark points is directly labelled, with subdued grid lines and a strong reference baseline; an N.D. strip records unobserved candidates below the axis.

unverified_boundaries: The x-axis in 5A is a set of metrics, not time; the profile cannot be cited as a time-course example.
Low-density dark points and clear solid lines are compatible with a polished figure; transparency is not mandatory for every mark.
Locally pinned author code is a preprint revision; it is not proof of final published Fig.5 renderer or values.
transfer_suggestion: Use full-strength primary curves when sparse; reserve fading for individual observations, uncertainty, or secondary context.
Combine color with line type when groups and cohorts are different variables.
Place uncertainty or missingness explicitly in labels/keys; do not fade missing values into invisibility.

metadata.title: Chromatin and gene-regulatory dynamics of the developing human cerebral cortex at single-cell resolution
metadata.metadata_verification: Current PubMed original-article record confirms 184(19):5053-5069.e23, print 16 September 2021 and epub 13 August 2021. Author repository README binds publication DOI.

figure_observation.method: Read-only Poppler rendering using pdftoppm -f 7 -l 7 -r 130 -singlefile -png; rendered whole PDF page inspected with functions.view_image

observations.observation: A strong red-to-blue focal pseudotime region sits inside a pale gray global embedding; the mapped version in B is lighter and less visually dense than A.
Compact dot matrices use size and color quantitatively; matching marker-size and color keys are positioned under the relevant matrices.
Small colored gene points use direct black labels and occupy an independent compact scatter, preserving readability without a cloud-wide dark stroke.

author_layers.binding: Author Louvain projection workflow verified; exact Figure 3A/B final assembly not bound.
Related projection-transfer arrows, not claimed as Figure 3 rendered layers.

unverified_boundaries: Author-hosted PDF is labelled article-in-press and has provisional pagination; bibliography is verified against final PubMed record.
Do not report alpha 0.3 as the measured Figure 3 point alpha; it is confirmed for a related author workflow.
The dot-matrix quantitative color scale must be evaluated with its legend and consistent opacity.
transfer_suggestion: Opacity can subordinate cluster points to centroid labels; override legend alpha to keep categorical keys readable.
Use pale global context around the focal lineage, without implying that light cells are less reliable.
Keep dense point layers light enough to expose overlap and strong enough to retain rare populations; avoid all-point heavy outlines.

transfer_rules: Choose opacity by visual role and overlap at final physical size.
Separate fill and edge opacity for moderate count observations.
Use thin or absent outlines for very dense cell clouds.
Keep summary lines, axes, text, and reference marks readable.
Use weaker interval or context fills below stronger foreground layers.
Match quantitative color semantics to the actual colorbar; retain alpha=1 by default.
Use clear categorical legend keys even when observations are translucent.
Preserve all observations, coordinate scales, sample identities and statistical meaning.
Distinguish pale RGB colors from actual transparency, and code utility settings from exact final-panel bindings.
